canonical.title: Take-home deployment for non-technical workshop participants

parent.title: Vibe coding workshop playbook (2-3 h, laymen, 2026)

siblings.title: Workshop-scale app ideas for laymen
siblings.summary: Five reliable app-idea menus that a non-developer can ship in 2-3 hours with an AI builder, plus the failure modes to swap out.

siblings.title: Vibe-coding tool stack on shared wifi, low budget
siblings.summary: Lovable as the default with Bolt.new as the backup, hosted hotspot for wifi, $0-$50 host spend for 20 attendees, and signup done the night before.

siblings.title: Prompting workflow: ChatGPT-refine -> Lovable-build
siblings.summary: A two-step workshop recipe - plan a structured PRD in ChatGPT (free, no credits burned), then paste it once into Lovable's Agent mode to seed the build.

siblings.title: Facilitation logistics and failure modes
siblings.summary: The pre-flight checklist, room/tool fallbacks, and the failure modes that actually sink 2-3 hour vibe coding workshops.

sources.title: Lovable pricing and credits (Banani)
sources.claim: Lovable's free tier gives 5 daily credits, 30/month max, up to 5 public projects hosted on lovable.app subdomains and no custom domains or private projects

sources.title: Lovable - Pricing
sources.claim: Lovable's pricing page positions the free plan as 'Start for free' with Pro tier unlocking private projects and custom domains

sources.title: Bolt.new - Hosting FAQ
sources.claim: Bolt.new ships a Publish button that deploys to Bolt Cloud by default; URL editing is paid-only

sources.title: Bolt.new free tier guide (getaiperks)
sources.claim: Bolt.new free tier in 2026 grants 1M tokens/month with no credit card required, sufficient for 2-5 small apps or one mid-size MVP

sources.title: Bolt.new hosting review (agentrank)
sources.claim: Every Bolt.new project now publishes to a free .bolt.host subdomain in roughly 10 seconds with HTTPS

sources.title: v0 - Pricing
sources.claim: v0 by Vercel free tier provides $5 in monthly credits that reset each billing cycle and deploys via one-click to Vercel Hobby hosting

sources.title: v0 by Vercel complete guide 2026 (nxcode)
sources.claim: v0 deploys directly to Vercel with one click for internal testing or production, with GitHub sync and env-var import on the free plan

sources.title: Replit limitations (p0stman)
sources.claim: Replit's free tier apps sleep after 5 minutes of inactivity with 10-30 second cold starts, get only a replit.app subdomain, and cannot run Always-On without the $20/month Core plan

sources.title: Claude Artifacts - Publishing
sources.claim: Claude Artifacts publishes to a permanent claude.ai URL that anyone can view without a Claude account

sources.title: Claude Artifacts limitations (p0stman)
sources.claim: Claude Artifacts cannot be pointed at a custom domain or used as production apps

sources.title: Base44 pricing (websitebuilderexpert)
sources.claim: Base44's free tier allows 5 messages/day and 25 messages/month with 500 integration credits

sources.title: Create.xyz - Publish docs
sources.claim: Create.xyz lets free-tier users publish from inside the app to a .created.app URL with built-in hosting and live preview

sources.title: Tempo review (vibecoding.app)
sources.claim: Tempo offers a free-forever plan with up to 50 GPT-4/Claude prompts, one-click deploys, and full export to Vercel/Netlify

sources.title: Bolt vs Replit vs Lovable (Lovable guide)
sources.claim: Lovable auto-syncs to GitHub for export while Bolt publishes to native bolt.host by default and Replit binds you to its own runtime that sleeps without a paid plan

sources.title: Lovable docs - Custom domain
sources.claim: Lovable apps deploy on a free *.lovable.app subdomain that remains as a permanent fallback even after a custom domain is attached

sources.title: Bolt - Domains
sources.claim: Bolt publishes every project to a free *.bolt.host subdomain immediately, with custom domains gated to paid plans

sources.title: Netlify - Get started with domains
sources.claim: Netlify gives every site a free *.netlify.app subdomain and attaching a custom domain is free on any plan

sources.title: Replit docs - Custom domains
sources.claim: Replit deployments get a free *.replit.app subdomain with auto-SSL, but linking a custom domain requires a Core/Pro/Enterprise paid plan

sources.title: Replit docs - Domain purchasing
sources.claim: Replit ships a one-click Domain Purchasing flow inside the platform that searches, buys, and auto-configures DNS

sources.title: Vercel Domains
sources.claim: Vercel Domains sells domains at registrar cost (no markup) with instant availability search and one-click attach

sources.title: Vercel docs - Add a domain
sources.claim: Free Hobby accounts allow up to 50 custom domains per project

sources.title: Cloudflare Registrar
sources.claim: Cloudflare Registrar sells .com domains at the wholesale price of $10.44/year with zero markup, free WHOIS privacy, and free DNSSEC

sources.title: Porkbun - Domains
sources.claim: Porkbun registers and renews .com at approximately $10.91/year with near-identical registration/renewal pricing

sources.title: is-a.dev
sources.claim: is-a.dev gives developers a free *.is-a.dev subdomain with Cloudflare-backed DNS and SSL, registered by opening a pull request on GitHub

sources.title: js-org/js.org
sources.claim: js.org offers free *.js.org subdomains via a four-step GitHub PR submission, but only accepts JavaScript-related projects

sources.title: Replit blog - Domain purchasing
sources.claim: Replit's in-platform domain purchasing supports .com, .ai and other popular TLDs and bundles auto-DNS configuration

sources.title: Supabase - Pricing
sources.claim: Supabase Free tier projects are paused after 1 week (7 days) of inactivity

sources.title: travisvn/supabase-pause-prevention
sources.claim: Community keep-alive tools (GitHub Actions cron pingers) exist specifically to work around Supabase pause-on-inactivity

sources.title: Vercel - Hobby plan docs
sources.claim: Vercel Hobby has no inactivity-based suspension; deployments persist indefinitely

sources.title: Render - Platforms with a real free tier 2026
sources.claim: On Render's free tier, web services spin down after 15 minutes of inactivity and take roughly one minute to restart

sources.title: Render free tier cold-start (samkiel.dev)
sources.claim: The Render cold-start UX failure is exactly the 'show grandma' problem: visitors see a dead-looking screen for 30-50 seconds

sources.title: Render changelog - Free Postgres 30-day expiry
sources.claim: Render's free PostgreSQL databases now expire 30 days after creation, with a 14-day grace period before deletion

sources.title: Railway - Pricing plans
sources.claim: Railway has no permanent free tier - only a 30-day trial with $5 credit and a credit card required at signup

sources.title: Fly.io free tier 2026 (saaspricepulse)
sources.claim: Fly.io no longer has a free tier for new signups in 2026; only a 2-VM-hour or 7-day trial

sources.title: Cloudflare Workers - Pricing
sources.claim: Cloudflare Workers/Pages free tier gives 100,000 requests/day with no cold starts (V8 isolates start in under 5ms)

sources.title: Neon docs - Scale to zero
sources.claim: Neon Postgres free tier always scales to zero after 5 minutes of inactivity, but resumes within a few hundred milliseconds

sources.title: PlanetScale free tier removed (codu)
sources.claim: PlanetScale removed its free Hobby tier in April 2024; cheapest entry is $5/month

sources.title: Turso - Pricing
sources.claim: Turso's free tier is always-on with no pause-on-inactivity (9 GB storage)

sources.title: Netlify - Pricing
sources.claim: Netlify free plan does not suspend for inactivity, only for exceeding the 100 GB bandwidth / 300 build minutes quota

sources.title: Lovable blog - Mobile app
sources.claim: Lovable mobile app syncs projects between phone and desktop so a user can pick up exactly where they left off

sources.title: Lovable launches mobile app (TechCrunch)
sources.claim: Lovable launched a free iOS and Android mobile app on April 27, 2026

sources.title: Lovable Google signin tutorial (nocode.mba)
sources.claim: Lovable supports sign-in via Google, GitHub, or email and uses that identity to manage the dashboard

sources.title: Lovable blog - Versioning 2.0
sources.claim: Lovable's Versioning 2.0 groups edits by date like Google Docs, adds bookmarks for milestone versions

sources.title: Lovable docs - Plans and credits
sources.claim: Lovable's free plan gives 5 daily credits up to a maximum of 30 per calendar month

sources.title: Bolt - Rollback and backup
sources.claim: Bolt.new keeps a version history timeline and restoring an earlier version does not change the current Bolt or Supabase databases

sources.title: v0 - FAQ
sources.claim: v0 retains conversation context and chat history across sessions so iteration builds on prior state

sources.title: Vercel v0 pricing explained (uibakery)
sources.claim: v0's free plan gives $5 in monthly credits with a 7-message-per-day cap

sources.title: Replit blog - Mobile apps
sources.claim: Replit Mobile Apps lets users go from idea to a published native iOS app via Replit Agent on a phone

sources.title: Replit iPhone app update delay (9to5mac)
sources.claim: Replit's iPhone vibe-coding app went four months without updates due to an App Store review dispute

sources.title: Replit guide (deployhq)
sources.claim: Replit supports continuous deployment where every change pushed to GitHub from the Version Control tab triggers an automatic redeployment

sources.title: Best vibe-coding tools 2026 (vybe.build)
sources.claim: Most vibe-coding tools generate code and hand it over rather than maintain the running app

sources.title: Keep Supabase free tier active (Medium)
sources.claim: Supabase free-tier projects auto-pause after 7 days of database inactivity, and dashboard visits do not count as activity

sources.title: Keep Supabase live past the limit (aiagencyplus)
sources.claim: When a Supabase free project is paused the data and schema are preserved, but reactivation takes ~30 seconds

sources.title: Supabase GitHub discussion #38950
sources.claim: Real users on GitHub report Supabase projects stuck in paused state with the unpause button failing for over an hour

sources.title: Supabase GitHub issue #43038
sources.claim: Free-tier Supabase users have reported projects stuck in a 'Pausing...' state indefinitely

sources.title: Vercel - Is SQLite supported?
sources.claim: Vercel officially states SQLite cannot be used with their platform because serverless storage is ephemeral

sources.title: Replit docs - SQL database
sources.claim: Replit migrated its built-in database off Neon to its own managed Postgres on December 4, 2025, with 20GB free storage

sources.title: Replit blog - Replspace filesystems
sources.claim: Writes to a deployed Repl's local filesystem do not persist across redeploys

sources.title: Lovable Cloud docs
sources.claim: Lovable Cloud bundles database, auth, storage and AI auto-provisioned per workspace with $25 monthly cloud credit

sources.title: Bolt Cloud announcement
sources.claim: Bolt Cloud bundles managed databases, native auth, file storage and hosting into one no-config product

sources.title: Vibe-eval - Lovable safety report
sources.claim: Lovable apps routinely embed third-party API keys (Stripe, OpenAI, SendGrid, analytics) directly into the JavaScript bundle

sources.title: Vibe-coding security risks (modall)
sources.claim: In March 2026, 1.5 million API keys were leaked from a single vibe-coded app

sources.title: Anthropic OAuth ban (laozhang.ai)
sources.claim: On April 4, 2026 Anthropic banned subscription OAuth tokens in third-party tools

sources.title: Clerk pricing guide (supertokens)
sources.claim: Clerk's free tier in 2026 covers 50,000 Monthly Active Users with unlimited social logins

sources.title: Clerk docs - Production deployment
sources.claim: Clerk ships separate development and production instance keys; common deployment failure is forgetting to swap

sources.title: Google OAuth invalid grant (Nango)
sources.claim: Google OAuth refresh tokens expire after just 7 days while the consent screen is in Testing mode

sources.title: Vibe coding workshop insights (Benzatine)
sources.claim: Debugging is the single biggest stumbling block for non-technical workshop participants

sources.title: Vibe coding failures (autonoma)
sources.claim: Across 170 Lovable-built apps shipped by beginners, authorization was inverted so unauthenticated visitors had full data access

sources.title: Lovable community
sources.claim: Lovable's primary continuity pattern is a 160K-member Discord plus recurring topical office hours and a community@lovable.dev email

sources.title: Berkeley ALS vibe coding
sources.claim: Facilitators at the Berkeley ALS vibe-coding sessions concluded that one workshop is never enough and committed to a series of follow-up workshops

sources.title: 8 vibe coding mistakes (buildtolaunch)
sources.claim: Two failure modes that matter most: exposed databases and 'works on my machine = shipped' assumptions

sources.title: We vibe-coded our way to nowhere (Medium)
sources.claim: A 2026 hackathon retrospective documents the canonical post-event failure: prototypes that 'looked done but weren't'

sources.title: Anthropic - Teach For All
sources.claim: Anthropic's Teach For All program codifies the post-workshop stack: monthly office hours plus Claude Connect across 60+ countries

sources.title: Vibe Coders Collective (Meetup)
sources.claim: The Vibe Coders Collective shows in-person workshop afterlife typically runs on Meetup + a hub site + LinkedIn
